3D bake houses (owner 2026-09-21, density v4 — 'pack the houses tighter, and shrink the bare brown ground disc'): the house cluster's share of the BUILT GROUND's radius, so a settlement's footprint is r_house / this and the ring from the last house out to the footprint's edge is built ground with no houses on it (定居点周边和地图上的地形要有一定距离的缓冲过渡). It replaces house_radius_ratio, which pointed the other way: the footprint came from population and the houses took a share of it, so shrinking the disc only forced that share up and cancelled the shrink (density v2). The cluster is the primitive now; the disc is derived from it. 0.53 is not a free look choice. The footprint mask fades from 1 at 0.3 of its radius to 0 at its edge, and a house candidate needs foot >= house_foot_min (0.55), which lands at 0.53 of the radius on average — so a cluster wider than that simply has its outer ring refused, which is the whole of the difference measured over the real pack at IDENTICAL cluster radii: 0.53 gives 87-93% of every group's target placed and 24 of 684 settlements reduced to their landmark alone, while the 0.78 first proposed gives 78-82% and 36. Raising it means lowering house_foot_min in step, or the cluster is truncated and the outer ring quotas are spent inward

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2 (spec 2026-09-20): a flat count budget spent by a single greedy nearest-first fill cuts a hard circle — full density, then nothing, however far short of r_house that budget runs out (measured: a capital's fill stopped at 220 m of its own 342 m). The group's target is instead split into this many concentric ring quotas (richest at the centre, thinning by house_edge_falloff_gamma), so the outermost ring still gets a nonzero share and the cluster is built to reach near r_house rather than exhaust itself in one dense core. If real terrain leaves a ring short of its own quota (a shore, a slope, a small island), bake_houses.place() spends the shortfall on whatever ring still has room rather than leaving it unbuilt, so the group's target is still reached wherever the settlement's own ground allows it

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2: how hard the ring quotas thin from centre to rim — weight(ring) = (1 - ring's own mid-radius fraction) ^ this, so 1.0 is a straight linear taper and higher values spend more of the budget on the core, leaving the rim sparser still (a NEW gamma, unrelated to the removed house_density_gamma: that one scattered points with no lanes at all and was rejected outright; this one only grades how a FIXED total spends its ring quotas across a network that already has its own negative space from the lanes)

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 1: lane frontage was supplying essentially the whole per-group target before block fill ever got a slot (measured: 399 of a capital's 400), so the town read as a starburst of strings with empty wedges between the lanes. Caps what the frontage pass may take of EACH ring's own quota to this share, reserving the rest for block fill — most of a medieval town's buildings sit behind the street frontage, not on it. Applied within the ring-quota system (a share of quotas[ring], not of the flat total) so the edge feathering is unaffected; if capping frontage leaves a ring's remainder unfillable by infill (small blocks, refusing terrain), the leftover pass lets frontage take it back rather than lose it

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a small or narrow site (a harbour village whose buildable land is a sliver, most of its r_house being open water) can leave a settlement at just its landmark plus one house — not from lack of room, but because the plot_step_m infill grid never happens to land a candidate in the sliver that IS buildable (measured on one such village: 4 of 96 candidates passed at the normal 10 m step, 49 of ~1500 at a third of it). Only spent as a last-resort top up once every other pass has left the settlement short of its target, so it changes nothing for a settlement that already reaches its target

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a second, separate cause found on a real settlement (chawbigdon, a city) -- not water, not slope (both clear everywhere in its disc), but the footprint/built-ground mask itself sat at ~0.48 at the settlement's OWN centre and fell further outward, on land otherwise flat and dry (bake_world.py's own footprint_edge_noise fraying low across this one disc, out of this module's reach). The absolute last resort: house_foot_min scaled by this ratio, tried only once the fine grid above has ALSO failed. Never touches the shore or slope tests, so a genuinely steep or wet site (verified separately: apton, aringham -- 100% slope failures well past the threshold) is still correctly left at its landmark
